entities.summary:
Black January, also known as Black Saturday or the January Massacre, was a violent crackdown on Azerbaijani nationalism and anti-Soviet sentiment in Baku on 19–20 January 1990, as part of a state of emergency during the dissolution of the Soviet Union. 

 This event was a pivotal moment in the modern history of Azerbaijan, marking a turning point in the struggle for independence from Soviet rule. Led by the Soviet-backed government of Azerbaijan, the crackdown resulted in the deaths of over 100 people and the wounding of hundreds more. 

 The aftermath of Black January saw a significant shift in the political landscape of Azerbaijan, with the rise of nationalist and anti-Soviet sentiment. The event also had far-reaching consequences for the Soviet Union, contributing to its eventual dissolution. 

 In the years following Black January, Azerbaijan continued to assert its independence, with the country eventually gaining full independence in 1991. The legacy of Black January serves as a powerful reminder of the human cost of conflict and the enduring power of national identity.
